reviews.body: The core change looks correct and internally consistent: `openai` and `openai_responses` now default to `gpt-5.6-sol` with the retiring `gpt-5`/`gpt-5-mini` entries removed from their lists, the `codex` exclusion is explained, and the new regression test pins the retirement. TDD requirement is satisfied with the added test. I left one verification question (chat-completions tool routing for the new default under the pinned langchain-openai, given the gpt-6 precedent in `models/factory.py`), one missed occurrence (`openai/gpt-5-mini` in the openrouter provider), and two small follow-ups/nits.

review_comments.body: Please confirm `gpt-5.6-sol` accepts function tools on `/v1/chat/completions`. The pinned langchain-openai only forces the Responses API for its `_RESPONSES_API_ONLY_PREFIXES` tuple (gpt-5-pro-style names), so this provider (which sets no `use_responses_api`) sends `gpt-5.6-sol` through chat completions. The repo already had to backport a gpt-6-family fix for exactly this failure mode — OpenAI rejecting function tools on that endpoint (see the `_apply_openai_responses_api_default` comment in `backend/packages/harness/deerflow/models/factory.py`). If the gpt-5.6 family behaves like gpt-6, every tool call in a wizard-generated `openai` config would 400.

Same retirement rationale, one spot missed: the `openrouter` provider further down in this file still offers `openai/gpt-5-mini` in its `models` list. If OpenAI shuts gpt-5-mini down on 2026-12-11, OpenRouter's proxy of it presumably goes too. The PR description explains why `codex` is excluded but not `openrouter` — consider swapping it for `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` or noting why it stays.

The same 2026-12-11 retirement still applies to `gpt-5` references outside the wizard: the commented-out example at `config.example.yaml:316-319` (`model: gpt-5`), and the `gpt-5-responses` snippets in `README.md` plus its translations, `backend/README.md`/`backend/README_zh.md`, and `backend/docs/CONFIGURATION.md`. Cheap follow-up if you want the whole repo consistent; otherwise fine to leave for a separate docs pass.

Nit: this could assert on `openai.default_model` instead of hard-coding `"gpt-5.6-sol"`, so the test keeps passing at the next default bump — the new retirement test below already reads `default_model` dynamically. Also, the new test's docstring mentions gpt-5/gpt-5-mini/gpt-5-nano but the `retiring` set additionally contains `gpt-5-pro`; harmless, just noting the mismatch.

comments.body:
Follow-up to review on #7923.

- OpenRouter model list in the setup wizard: `openai/gpt-5-mini` -> `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` (gpt-5-mini retires 2026-12-11).
- `test_setup_wizard.py`: the OpenAI extra_config assertion now uses `openai.default_model` instead of a hardcoded model name; docstring now also lists gpt-5-pro.

On function tools over `/v1/chat/completions`: OpenAI's model page for gpt-5.6-sol (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol) lists Chat Completions as a supported endpoint and function calling as a supported feature, with no Responses-only restriction. The gpt-6 pages carry an explicit note ("Use the Responses API for built-in tools and function calling. Chat Completions supports function calling only with `reasoning_effort` set to `none`"), which is what `_apply_openai_responses_api_default` handles; gpt-5.6-sol has no such note, so no `use_responses_api` override is added here. This is based on the docs, not a live call.

The remaining `gpt-5` mentions in config.example.yaml, the READMEs and CONFIGURATION.md are left for a separate docs pass, as suggested.

Wizard tests: 52 passed.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
